format: light_table v1 (clouds/embed/compile/light_table.py). Per sun elevation elevations[i] (degrees, ascending): E_sun_lut[i] = 32 RGB triples flattened to 96 numbers [r0, g0, b0, r1, ...], sun irradiance at altitude y = lut_y0 + k * lut_dy (m), disk-averaged, 0 in Earth's shadow; L_sky[i] = RGB mean upper-hemisphere sky radiance seen from l_sky_altitude (m); L_gnd[i] = RGB ground radiance at 0 m, albedo/pi * (E_sun(0) max(s.y, 0) + E_sky). Interpolate linearly in elevation, clamp at the ends; exception: L_sky and L_gnd geometrically (linear in log) on the 1-degree segments below -6 degrees, where they fall ~5x per degree (linear: up to 28 % error mid-segment; geometric: 1.2 %). RGB = 680, 550, 440 nm, same units as the references (E_TOA = 20).
